title: Learning peripheral regional anesthesia with and without help of AI-guided sonography (NERVEBLOX)
summary: In this study, the aim is to determine whether the support provided by artificial intelligence (AI) during ultrasound guidance can facilitate the learning and execution of peripheral regional anaesthesia procedures. Trainee doctors with limited prior experience perform peripheral nerve blocks either with or without the use of the AI-assisted software NerveBlox® according to a defined protocol. The objective is to assess whether computer-aided image analysis increases user satisfaction and enhances the learning process. Following each procedure, questionnaires are completed to evaluate both the overall experience and the technical implementation, with all procedures conducted under expert supervision to ensure patient safety.

interventions.name: Participants learn peripheral regional anesthesia with the assistance of AI-supported sonography on the upper extremity, while it is performed on the lower extremity without AI support.
Participants learn peripheral regional anesthesia with the assistance of AI-supported sonography on the lower extremity, while it is performed on the upper extremity without AI support.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Doctors in training for the specialist qualification in anesthesiology at the study center.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent for participation; prior training in ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia.
